readMe:
THIS FILE IS STEP 1 OF tools/loop/ITERATION-PROMPT.md AND IT MUST STAY READABLE IN ONE Read.
STEP 1 READS THREE FILES, NOT ONE: this file, GATES.md, and PLAN.md §14. All three go through a Read
that has TWO ceilings: it TRUNCATES past 25,000 tokens and FAILS OUTRIGHT past 256 KB. BOTH HAVE
ALREADY BITTEN THIS FILE. iter127 hit the byte ceiling - the Read was refused, 459 KB, because the
`done` log had reached 397 KB of it. iter128 found the TOKEN cap had been truncating for longer and
unnoticed: at 74,115 bytes / 31,303 tokens, step 1 returned lines 1-43 of 92 and dropped `decisions`
(the six outstanding decisions), `doneCount`, `doneArchive`, `doneRecent` and `spikes`.

CORRECTED AT ITER129, because a later method depends on it: TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT. The tool prints
"[Truncated: PARTIAL view - showing lines 1-462 of 1500 total (68900 tokens, cap 25000)]". iter128
called truncation "the worse failure because it looks like success"; the real risk is an agent
SKIMMING PAST an explicit notice, not the tool hiding anything. That notice is also the ONLY tokenizer
on this machine (no tiktoken, no anthropic, no transformers), and it is how iter129 calibrated the
size checker: build a file over the cap but under 256 KB, Read it whole, divide bytes by the reported
total. Markdown measured 2.604 B/tok, this file's JSON 2.368.

RUN `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` AFTER EVERY EDIT TO THIS FILE, TO GATES.md, OR TO PLAN.md.
It measures ALL THREE step-1 files (iter128's version measured only this one), prints each file's
HEADROOM IN KB before it truncates, distinguishes the two ceilings, lists this file's largest fields,
flags every other tools/loop file, and EXITS NON-ZERO when something stops fitting.
WHEN IT TRIPS ON THIS FILE: move an append-heavy field into an archive under tools/loop/ and leave a
short pointer behind. There are EIGHT precedents - `doneArchive`, `blockersArchive`, `gatesArchive`,
`methodNotes`, `scratchInventory`, `spikesArchive`, `decisions._archive` (iter130, the one that
keeps its pointer INSIDE the field it drained rather than as a sibling key), and `doneRecent`
(iter151, drained to empty because every entry was already in done-archive.jsonl - see
`doneRecentNote`, and do not refill it) - and each one asserted
its round-trip before this file was rewritten. Do not discard content to make the check pass. WHEN IT TRIPS ON GATES.md OR
PLAN.md: that content is the spec and the gate instructions, so archive a settled section, never drop
one.

AND NOTE WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS AT THE TOP OF THE FILE RATHER THAN NEXT TO `doneArchive`: a truncated
Read still shows it. iter127's rotation rule was correct and had no effect, because it was written
into a field that sat past the cut. A rule that keeps a file readable is worthless in the half that
gets cut off.
phase:
M6 feature-complete. **ITER156 ANSWERED THE FACTUAL HALF OF AN OPEN DECISION THAT HAD BEEN WAITING ON MIRKO SINCE ITER113 — WITHOUT DECIDING IT.** decisions.mermaidDialectGap is still his three-way call and the loop did not pick one. But GATES.md's option (a) read "upgrade or replace beautiful-mermaid (check whether a later version takes `graph TD;` and `pie`)", and that parenthesis was a question of FACT sitting inside a question of JUDGEMENT. It is now measured, and three of the four findings change which option a reasonable person picks.

  (1) **The upgrade half of (a) is a dead end**: 1.1.3 IS `dist-tags.latest`, ten versions, time.modified 2026-02-26. The gate had offered a nonexistent upgrade for 43 iterations. (2) **The gap is 17 diagram types, not 1** — six families supported (10/10 spellings render), 0 of 18 other mermaid v11 spellings do, and the set is closed by construction rather than by sampling. (3) **The semicolon rejection is an inconsistency INSIDE the library** — its own detectDiagramType splits on /[\n;]/ and already tolerates it, parseMermaid does not — so (b) completes a half-implemented tolerance rather than overriding a design stance. 9/9 predicted. (4) **NEW: YAML frontmatter fails on every type including the six that work**, which no option in the gate addresses.

  **THE DOCS WERE CORRECTED IN THE SAME SLICE, AND A TRIPWIRE CAUGHT THE LOOP OVER-CLAIMING.** conversion.md had written iter113's four-case sample up as a two-row denylist, which reads as though `pie` were an exception; it now states a closed six-family allowlist and scopes the semicolon row to graph/flowchart/stateDiagram. **The frontmatter finding is prose under that table, NOT a third row, and the suite is why.** Adding the row went green on build and on GapsPageTests and turned the full suite red: MermaidAcceptanceTests.The_conversion_page_names_exactly_the_headers_the_real_renderer_rejects renders every row through the real renderer and fails any row the GOLDEN CORPUS does not reject ("warns a reader off a diagram that works"). No golden case carries frontmatter, so a measured-elsewhere fact reads as an over-claim — correctly. The table stayed at two rows, the test was NOT weakened, and GapsPageTests instead grew an assertion binding the frontmatter sentence on BOTH pages so the third fact is still held. Lesson in method-notes.md.

  Verified: build 0/0; run-suite.py **1388/1388 twice**, at HEAD before any write and again after the last write, because this iteration edited four `.md` files and the prose sweeps are exactly what a docs-only edit turns red. **The iter154 flake did NOT reproduce; it is still unnamed, and that is still the honest state.**
nextAction:
**RUN `dotnet build` AND `python3 tools/loop/run-suite.py` BEFORE YOU CHANGE ANYTHING, AND AGAIN AFTER YOUR LAST WRITE. USE run-suite.py, NOT `dotnet test | tail`** (iter154): `tail` keeps the summary and drops the failure lines above it, so a red suite becomes a bare number. It leaves a log + TRX in `.mtk/suite-runs/` (gitignored), prints failing ids with their assertion messages, drops the artifacts on green, mirrors the exit code, and takes `--repeat N` for a flake hunt. Several tests sweep the tree's own prose (RepositorySlugTests over `*.md`/`*.yml`/`*.json` outside `tests/` and `tools/`, QuickstartTests over fenced commands), so a docs-only edit — GATES.md included — can turn it red. **`dotnet test --nologo` RUNS ZERO TESTS AND EXITS 1**; plain `dotnet test` is the command. One class is `dotnet test --filter-query '/*/*/<Class>/*'`, **ONE pattern only** (`a|b` exits 1, `(a|b)` exits 8, `--treenode-filter` is dead — iter143).

**FIRST, RUN `git diff tools/loop/state.json` AND `git status`. AN ANSWER FROM MIRKO ARRIVES AS AN UNCOMMITTED EDIT TO THIS FILE** — that is how iter155 found `decisions.formatOnEditHook`. **Trust the `decisions` and `gates` fields plus GATES.md's checkboxes over any prose in `phase`/`nextAction`**, which are written an iteration earlier and go stale the moment Mirko replies.

**BEFORE YOU END ON WAITING-GATE, RE-READ THE GATE PROSE FOR EMBEDDED VERBS — *check*, *find out*, *see whether*, *confirm*. THAT IS THE LOOP'S WORK WEARING A GATE'S CLOTHES, AND IT IS HOW ITER156 FOUND ITS INCREMENT** after four iterations had read the same sentence and seen only "Mirko's call". The judgement in a decision is his; the facts inside the sentence describing it are the loop's. `decisions.mermaidDialectGap`'s option (a) had said "check whether a later version takes `graph TD;` and `pie`" since iter113; `npm view beautiful-mermaid versions` answered it in 30 seconds and the answer was no. **The remaining six open decisions have not been swept this way — do that before concluding there is nothing to do.** The four `planSection*` ones in particular gate PLAN.md prose edits the loop is otherwise able to make, and each has a test that fails on an empty deviation list ON PURPOSE: read the assertion message before touching it.

**THEN CHECK GATES.md. TEN BOXES ARE UNCHECKED AND ALL TEN ARE MIRKO'S:** five milestone gates (m2, m3, m4, m5, m6) and five side items (paste-rule-8-2a, paste-force-push-hook, settings-corrections, paste-format-on-edit-hook, restart-loop-driver). **`python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` FAILS IF THE `gates` MIRROR STOPS MATCHING THOSE BOXES, INCLUDING ON STATUS DRIFT** — trust the checker over the prose. Cheapest first: restart-loop-driver (three commands; iter140 tested what it activates, 9/9, nothing pending), gate-m3 (add one `approved` label), gate-m4 (write one wrong comment), gate-m5 (answer decisions.m5Acceptance), gate-m2 (walk the 44 pages), gate-m6 (push main, then tag v0.1.0).

**DO NOT RE-MEASURE THE MERMAID SURFACE — iter156 did it and the probes are re-runnable** (`.mtk/paths-156/probe-mermaid-surface.py`, 39 dialects; `.mtk/paths-156/probe-semicolon-mechanism.py`, 13/13). The findings are in GATES.md under the mermaid block and summarised in `decisions.mermaidDialectGap`. **What is left there is Mirko picking (a-as-replace) / (b) / (c), plus deciding what to do about frontmatter, which no option covers.** The loop must not pick.

**paste-format-on-edit-hook IS A PURE PASTE — ITS QUESTION IS SETTLED, SO DO NOT RE-ASK IT AND DO NOT RECREATE `tools/hooks/format-on-edit.py`.** `decisions.formatOnEditHook` is "delete", CLOSED, loop's half shipped at iter155. **IF MIRKO HAS PASTED IT** — check that `.claude/settings.json` has no `hooks` key, do not assume; it still had one at iter156 — then `git add -- .claude/settings.json`, commit it, tick that box, move the mirror off PENDING, and archive both the gate item and the paste file. **The loop cannot write `.claude/`**: a path-based classifier sits above the permission layer. Do not retry it and do not route around it with an allowlisted `python3`.

**SEVEN DECISIONS ARE STILL OPEN, ALL MIRKO'S:** mermaidDialectGap (now fully measured, see above), m5Acceptance, pushPolicy, planSection5Deviations, planSection6Deviations, planSection9Deviation, planSection10Deviations.

**IF restart-loop-driver IS TICKED:** re-run `python3 .mtk/paths-139/probe-driver-version-drift.py` as the in-situ confirmation and expect cell A to go RED (driver now NEWER than the commit), with the next log line carrying `(pass N)` and `[model: ...]` and the log file named `iter-<n>-pass<NNNN>-<ts>.log`. **NO CODE CHANGE IS PENDING** — iter140 tested every function the restart wakes, 9/9. Expect ONE cosmetic change: `modelUsage` will read `claude-opus-5` instead of `claude-opus-5[1m]`, same canonicalModel / contextWindow / maxOutputTokens (measured).

**READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH tools/loop/docume-loop.sh.** It is the one file an iteration can edit but cannot make take effect: the running driver started 2026-07-24 14:38:30 and bash parses a `while` loop once. So check whether your 'fix' is already there and simply not running — as of iter140 the committed version is TESTED, so the prior is strongly that it is already correct. Live despite the staleness, because they are re-read by path every pass: ITERATION-PROMPT.md and loop-settings.json.

**HYGIENE, NOT URGENT, AND DO NOT DELETE IT WITHOUT ASKING:** `tests/golden/.claude/analytics.json` is untracked and was created 2026-07-24 20:31 by an MTK analytics write that ran with `tests/golden` as its cwd. It is a data file, so the global rule says ask before removing. It breaks nothing today (the suite is 1388/1388 with it present, and the prose sweeps exclude `tests/`), but `tests/golden/` is a rule §4.3 contract directory and a stray `.claude/` inside it is a trap for any future golden enumerator. Ask Mirko whether to delete it or gitignore it.

blockers._archive: FULL BLOCKER BODIES ARE IN tools/loop/blockers-open.json (moved at iter139; nothing discarded, round-trip asserted — the eighth archive precedent, and like decisions._archive the pointer stays INSIDE the field it drained). Each line below is ONE OPEN blocker: what it is, whose call it is, and where to answer. EVERY ONE IS PHRASED AS A QUESTION FOR MIRKO and every one is also written up at length in GATES.md, which step 1 reads anyway — so open the archive only to ACT on one. NOTE: tools/loop/blockers-archive.jsonl is a DIFFERENT file holding SETTLED blockers. **`blockers` IS AN OBJECT, NOT AN ARRAY** (matching `gates` and `decisions`; nothing reads it programmatically — checked). TO ADD ONE, per protocol step 9: a short kebab-case key here with a ONE-LINE stub ending in a pointer, and the full body in blockers-open.json under the same key. TO SETTLE ONE: delete the key from both, and append a one-line verdict to blockersArchive.settled so it is never re-added. (Condensed iter150 as budget payback; the historical justification for the iter139 move is in blockers-open.json and the done archive.)

gates.gate-m6-first-release: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and the only irreversible one - a package on a GitHub Packages feed cannot be unpublished, which is why the loop will not do it. Steps: (1) confirm Directory.Build.props <Version>, plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json version and plugin/README.md's git-subdir ref all read the number you want (all three read 0.1.0; release.yml's first step refuses a mismatch before building, so a wrong guess costs nothing); (2) `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`; (3) delete the 'Not published yet' note from README.md; (4) tick. The loop then walks the README literally in a fresh empty directory - that walk IS M6's acceptance. A PAT with read:packages in the loop environment is needed for the install half.

decisions.mermaidDialectGap: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter113 — **the JUDGEMENT is still his; the FACTS were measured at iter156 and the loop must not pick an option.** beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 renders six families and nothing else. Options unchanged: (a) upgrade-or-replace, (b) strip a trailing `;` in tools/render-mermaid.mjs, (c) report unsupported dialects as a named degradation instead of failing the page. **What iter156 added, and (1) kills half of (a):** (1) **NO LATER VERSION EXISTS** — 1.1.3 is `dist-tags.latest`, ten published, time.modified 2026-02-26, so (a) means REPLACE or nothing; the "check whether a later version takes `graph TD;` and `pie`" homework in the gate has been deleted because it is answered. (2) **THE GAP IS 17 TYPES, NOT 1** — 10/10 spellings of graph/flowchart, sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, erDiagram, stateDiagram/-v2 and xychart-beta render; 0 of 18 other mermaid v11 spellings do (pie, gantt, journey, gitGraph, mindmap, timeline, quadrantChart, requirementDiagram, C4Context, sankey-beta, block-beta, packet-beta, kanban, architecture-beta, radar-beta, treemap-beta, zenuml). Closed by construction: detectDiagramType (index.ts:54) has four branches + a flowchart default, parseMermaid (parser.ts:31) adds state diagrams. (3) **THE SEMICOLON IS AN INCONSISTENCY INSIDE THE LIBRARY, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES (b) CHEAP** — detectDiagramType splits on /[\n;]/ and ALREADY tolerates it (sequenceDiagram; classDiagram; erDiagram; xychart-beta; render), parseMermaid re-splits on \n alone so the ";" reaches the flowchart header regex's \s*$ (parser.ts:44) and graph TD; flowchart LR; graph TB; stateDiagram; stateDiagram-v2; fail. 9/9 predicted from source. (4) **NEW: YAML FRONTMATTER FAILS ON EVERY TYPE INCLUDING THE SIX THAT WORK** (Invalid mermaid header: "---"), 4/4 — mermaid v10+ standard, GitHub renders it, and **no option above addresses it**, so fold it into whichever you pick. Full write-up: GATES.md's mermaid block. Probes: .mtk/paths-156/probe-mermaid-surface.py (39 dialects) and probe-semicolon-mechanism.py (13/13). Historical body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json.

doneArchive.howToAppend: EVERY ITERATION: append one line to the archive with n = doneCount + 1 and bump doneCount. **DO NOT WRITE TO `doneRecent` - IT WAS DRAINED AT ITER151 AND STAYS EMPTY** (see `doneRecentNote`; the archive is the record, and refilling it re-spends the budget four iterations in a row had to scramble for). It was 5 until iter128 (which measured 8.5 KB in five entries against a state file that had to shed 27 KB), then 3, then 2; iter129 took it to 1 when the budget check tripped on its own prose and two long entries no longer fit. THE PATTERN IS THE POINT: the iteration that grows this file pays it back, rather than raising the budget to suit itself. ASSERT THE ENTRY YOU DROP IS ALREADY IN THE ARCHIVE before dropping it, and run `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` afterwards. THE ARCHIVE IS AUTHORITATIVE AND COMPLETE; doneRecent is a convenience tail and nothing more.
